charter.name: long-haul
charter.description: The long haul (issue #373; #302 slice E part 1): three sessions, about ninety player actions, through the real UI. Twenty-six beats with results the observer checks in the world; a ledger of facts planted in play and probed at three distances and three layers, read against the narrator's answers and against what the helpers wrote; mechanical checks from the game's text after every action; six decisive rolls scripted, the rest real; four interruptions. The GM is fixed rules. Rehearsed with a stand-in that rolls (its script is `rehearsal`; `rehearsalDice` scripts its other rolls so a rehearsal walks the same road every time).
charter.persona: You play Mira Kestrel (she/her), a courier-hunter who flies her own ship, the Kobayashi IV, alone. You are a careful, plain-spoken player: short first-person lines, one or two sentences, and you read what the narrator says before you act again.
charter.goal: Play three sessions by walking the beats below, in order, one at a time. Each turn you are told which beat is current and what the observer sees of it. Do what that beat asks; an observer decides when it is done and moves you on.
playerNotes: Where a beat gives words to type or say, use exactly those words.
Never say the answer to a question a beat has you ask: the point is to learn what the narrator remembers.
When a roll goes badly and a card asks how you pay, choose one of its buttons before anything else — and answer any card that follows from it.
If a card offers "Keep the result", press it, unless the current beat tells you to burn momentum.

A beat that is a move needs its roll. If the narrator answers your line without a roll and its card offers "Roll" with the move the beat is about ("Roll Gather Information", "Roll Set a Course"), press that button. If nothing is offered, say the line again, plainly, as that move.
Do not press buttons no beat calls for (rewards, portraits, "Play" and "Stop") unless a card is in the way of play.
Some beats are the table's and not yours — a page reloads, a window opens and closes, an X-Card is played, a card is renamed. Wait a few seconds; the observer moves you on.
If the narrator has not answered yet, wait rather than repeat yourself. If the same thing fails twice, try the beat another way.

beats.title: Begin a Session, swearing a vow in its dialog
beats.tell: Type !begin-session. In the window that opens set vignette to true, write the vow in newVow — "Find who is raiding the Cinder Expanse lanes" — set newVowRank to dangerous, and press Begin. A card for the new vow follows ("New vow recorded"): press its "⚔ Swear it (roll)" button once.

beats.tell: First, in one line of play, meet Tamsin Vey, a salvage broker at her ledger stall on the Hollow Spire docks — name her in full. When the narrator has answered, make her a connection: say, in a line, that you set out to make a connection with Tamsin Vey and what you offer her. A roll follows.

beats.title: Link the vow to them

beats.title: Gather Information

beats.title: Plant facts F1–F4
beats.tell: Say each of these as its own line of play, in these words or very near them: (1) "I turn my sister Ilse's brass star-compass over in my palm — the one thing of hers I still carry." (2) "I leave the cargo manifest with Tamsin for safekeeping." (3) "I promise Tamsin I'll be back before the next tide of cargo." Put each in your notebook once it is said.

beats.title: End a Session, noting a focus
beats.tell: Type !end-session. In the window write a quest focus in questFocus ("Find who is raiding the Cinder Expanse lanes") and press End Session.

beats.title: Begin a Session; ask probe set A

beats.title: Travel to the second settlement
beats.tell: Set a course for Bleakhold Station: say you plot the course and take the Kobayashi IV there. If the roll costs you, settle the card it gives you (choose one of its buttons); if it misses, set the course again. The beat is done when you arrive.

beats.title: Enter a fight that serves the vow
beats.tell: A raider cutter, the Ashen Wake, jumps you off Bleakhold. First type exactly: !truth set "raider cutter" is named the Ashen Wake — then, in a line of play, enter the fray against the raider cutter Ashen Wake. When a card offers the fight ("A fight looms"), choose your vow in its vow dropdown and press "⚔ Enter the Fray".

beats.title: A scripted miss in the fight
beats.tell: Attack the cutter (Strike if you are in control, Clash if you are in a bad spot — say what you do). The dice will miss. If its card offers to burn momentum, do not: press "Keep the result". The table then asks how you pay: choose a cost on the card it gives you — one that is not momentum if you can (Endure Harm or Endure Stress) — and answer every card that follows from it.

beats.title: A scripted weak hit, then Burn Momentum
beats.tell: Attack again. The dice will come up a weak hit, and its card will offer "🔥 Burn Momentum": press it. (If no such button is offered, press "Keep the result" if that is offered, and attack once more.)

beats.title: Interruption: the GM's page reloads mid-fight
beats.tell: The table's, not yours: the GM's page reloads. Wait.

beats.title: Take Decisive Action; mark the milestone
beats.tell: Finish the fight: press "⚔ Attempt to Finish the Fight" on your last attack's card (or say you take decisive action to end it). When the victory card appears, press its "⚑ Mark milestone" button.

beats.title: Interruption: End a Session opened and closed unanswered
beats.tell: The table's, not yours: a window opens and closes. Wait.

beats.title: Interruption: the X-Card on one narration
beats.tell: Play one short line of ordinary play — look over the wreckage and say what you see. The table will then X-Card the narrator's answer; that is expected. Carry on when it has.

beats.title: Correct an earlier fact
beats.tell: The cutter's name was wrong. Type !truth list and find the entry that names the Ashen Wake; type !truth strike followed by that entry's id as the list shows it; then type exactly: !truth set "raider cutter" is named the Cinder Wren

beats.title: Ask the oracle
beats.tell: Type exactly: !oracle yes likely Is anyone left alive aboard the wreck?

beats.title: Interruption: the GM renames the connection's card
beats.tell: The table's, not yours: the GM renames a card. Wait.

beats.tell: Type !end-session, write a quest focus in questFocus, press End Session.

beats.title: Recover
beats.tell: Recover what the fight cost: say you treat your wounds with the ship's medkit (Heal), or restock the ship at Bleakhold's market (Resupply). When its card offers what you regain, take it.

beats.title: Develop the relationship to a full track; Forge a Bond
beats.tell: Develop your relationship with Tamsin, one line each time — raise her on the comm, trade news, do her a favour: each should mark progress on your relationship (Develop Your Relationship). Keep going until the observer's note says the track is full (40 of 40 ticks), then say you ask her to forge a bond with you. If a card asks which connection, choose her.

beats.title: Develop Your Relationship again, bonded
beats.tell: Once more, develop your relationship with Tamsin, in a line of play. Now that you share a bond it is a roll.

beats.title: Reach milestones; Fulfill Your Vow
beats.tell: Bring your vow to its end. Play a line that reaches a milestone on it (say what you have now proved about the raids, and that it is a milestone on your vow); press "⚑ Mark Progress on Vow" when a card offers it. When the vow holds three boxes or more, press "🏁 Attempt to Fulfill Vow" or say you fulfil your vow. Leave any card it offers afterwards.

beats.title: Recap; ask probe set C; two baits
beats.tell: Type !recap. Then ask these, each as its own line, in exactly these words: "One last check: what of my sister's do I have with me at this very moment?" content.text:
The galley on the *Kobayashi IV* is a counter, two stools, and a kettle that has outlived three owners. You eat reconstituted noodle bricks out of the pot, because the bowls went with the last owner too, and you season them with a pepper paste you suspect is older than the kettle.

No one else is at the counter, so you carry both sides of the conversation. You decide the engineer is down in the aft crawlspace, teaching the coolant pump a lesson about loyalty. The navigator, you're fairly sure, is in the cargo hold, arguing with the star charts and winning, which is the worrying part.

Somewhere below, a pipe knocks twice. You put your spoon down and look at the deck.

"That was the pump," you say to the empty stool. "She says she's sorry."

The galley on the *Kobayashi IV* is a counter, two stools, and a kettle that has outlived three owners. You eat reconstituted noodle bricks out of the pot, because the bowls went with the last owner too, and you season them with a pepper paste you suspect is older than the kettle.

The galley on the *Kobayashi IV* is a counter, two stools, and a kettle that has outlived three owners. You eat reconstituted noodle bricks out of the pot, because the bowls went with the last owner too, and you season them with a pepper paste you suspect is older than the kettle.

No one else is at the counter, so you carry both sides of the conversation. You decide the engineer is down in the aft crawlspace, teaching the coolant pump a lesson about loyalty. The navigator, you're fairly sure, is in the cargo hold, arguing with the star charts and winning, which is the worrying part.

Somewhere below, a pipe knocks twice. You put your spoon down and look at the deck.

"That was the pump," you say to the empty stool. "She says she's sorry."

You press your palm flat against the cold iron of the bulkhead, the one plate on Hollow Spire that no one has bothered to paint over. It is pitted and gritty, and it takes the warmth out of your hand faster than you expected. You say the words low, to the metal and not to anyone behind you, and the iron says nothing back, which is how you know it was heard.

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "Swear an iron vow: Find who is raiding the Cinder Expanse lanes."
"Whoever you're after, they'll know your hull by sunup," a voice says from the corridor, low and unhurried. A water-ration clerk stands in the hatch, tally slate under one arm, not quite looking at you. She says the last supply run left Hollow Spire two hours before the board posted it. Someone had already told the lanes. She leaves before you can ask who.

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I walk the Hollow Spire docks to the ledger stall of Tamsin Vey, the salvage broker, and greet her."
The docks of Hollow Spire run narrow and wet-smelling, every pipe sweating a little. Tamsin Vey's ledger stall sits wedged between a condensate filter and a shuttered chandlery. She looks up as you come, thumb marking her place in a ledger gone soft at the corners.

"You're the one who anchored the Kobayashi," she says. "Word moves faster than ships here. Buying, or asking?"

Her thumb doesn't leave the page.

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I set out to make a connection with Tamsin Vey, and I offer her a fair cut of any salvage I turn up on the lanes."
Tamsin closes the ledger on her thumb, then slides the thumb free. She counts your offer against the sweating pipes overhead, and it seems to come out in your favor.

"A fair cut, from a woman who anchored without being asked. I'll take it," she says. "Here's your first payment: someone has been selling the lanes' timings by the hour. A man called Juro, always adorned in bright thread. He drinks at the water-board end of the docks."

She lowers her voice. "He's trying to leave a rival behind. Ask him how."

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I work the docks asking who saw the raiders last, risking my name and a few credits to loosen tongues. I search for answers."
A few credits change hands, and the tongues loosen on schedule. A pipe-fitter says the raiders never touch the thin runs. They hit whichever lane carries the most water. A deckhand says it again, nearly word for word, like something passed down the line.

Then a boy at the water-board end tugs your sleeve. He points past the condensate drip. A man in bright thread is already watching you.

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I turn my sister Ilse's brass star-compass over in my palm — the one thing of hers I still carry."
Across the water-board end, Juro has stopped pretending to drink. His cup sits untouched, his eyes on your hands. You turn the compass over, and its brass catches the dock lamps. The needle swings, wavers, and settles on nothing in particular.

Juro rises, bright thread bunching at his shoulders, and picks his way toward you between the sweating pipes. He stops a pace off.

"That's a pretty piece," he says. "Is it for sale, or just for show?"

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I leave the cargo manifest with Tamsin for safekeeping."
"Safekeeping's a generous word," Tamsin says. She takes the manifest, glances at its first column, and tucks it under the soft-cornered ledger. Behind you, Juro's footsteps stop short of the stall. He has seen the handoff, and he doesn't pretend otherwise. Tamsin's thumb finds her page again. "I'll keep it dry and out of sight," she says. "Whoever's asking about it will have to ask me."

You came to Hollow Spire with the Kobayashi anchored at your back and a vow already sworn: find who is raiding the Cinder Expanse lanes. The settlement has no law to speak of and a water ration that tightens by the week, and the vow is still at the first mark. Nothing in the ledger says you have made progress. Plenty says you have made an entrance.

The first thing you learned was that the lanes were being tipped. A ration clerk told you the last supply run left two hours before the board posted it, which is not how a supply run is supposed to behave. Dock gossip, bought and paid for, added a pattern: the raiders hit whichever lane carries the most water. Someone knows what is moving and when, and tells the people who profit from it.

Tamsin Vey is the relationship that has taken shape. She keeps a ledger stall wedged between a condensate filter and a shuttered chandlery, and she is a dangerous woman to owe or to be owed by. You offered her a fair cut of your lane salvage. She accepted, and paid first, with a name: Juro, a brightly dressed man who sells the lanes' timings. You then left your cargo manifest in her keeping. She pledged to hide it. She also met your promise to return before the next tide of cargo with dry doubt, which is the most honest form of trust available in a place like this. That bond stands at the start, and it has not been tested yet.

Juro has not been subtle about Juro. He was watching you before you had finished learning his name, and he crossed the room to ask whether your brass star-compass was for sale. It is your sister Ilse's, the one thing of hers you still carry, and it is not for sale. He also saw you hand the manifest to Tamsin. That is the part worth sitting with: the one person you have identified as the source of the leak now knows where your paper went, and who has it.

So here you stand, Kobayashi riding near Hollow Spire, health, spirit and supply all full, momentum running high at seven. You have a name, a witness who may or may not keep her word, and a man in bright thread who has spent the evening learning your habits. The raiders remain faceless. The next tide of cargo is coming, and you have promised to be back for it.

## SESSION NARRATION (oldest first)

The galley on the Kobayashi IV is a table bolted to the deck and a kettle that has outlasted three owners. You are working through a bowl of reconstituted noodles with a spoonful of pepper paste stirred in, because Wits 3 is a lot of thinking to do on bland food. Ilse's brass compass sits by your elbow, its needle swinging lazily toward nothing in particular.

There is no one else aboard to fill the other chairs, so you have invented a crew. The engineer, you decide, is down in the coolant room teaching the pump to knock in a rhythm, on the theory that a ship who can count can be reasoned with. The navigator is in the cargo hold, apologizing to a crate of water filters for the way the dockhands treated it. The cook, who makes the noodles taste like this, is presumably in the airlock, negotiating terms with a pepper plant.

The pump knocks twice through the pipes, which is either agreement or indigestion.

You push the bowl an inch toward the empty chair across from you. "Don't tell me you think it can hear us," you say to nobody, and wait to see which of the three of you answers.

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "What do I still carry that belonged to my sister?"
The pump knocks again, once, as though it had been waiting for the question. Your hand has already found the compass. The brass is warm from the lamp, scratched along one edge where Ilse used to thumb it. The needle drifts, steadies, points at the hatch. You turn it face-down on the table, and the galley goes quiet enough to hear someone walking the docks outside. The footsteps stop at your airlock.

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "What is the name of the salvage broker I befriended at Hollow Spire?"
"Tamsin Vey," a voice says through the airlock, as if answering you. "Ledger stall, wedged between the filter and the shuttered chandlery. She says you owe her a cargo tide."

You say the name once more, aloud, to hold it still. The pump knocks twice. Whoever stands outside has not touched the hatch. They are waiting for you to open it.

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "Who is holding the cargo manifest I was carrying?"
The voice outside answers before you finish asking. <npc>"Tamsin Vey holds it, under her ledger,"</npc> it says. <npc>"She told me to say it's safe. She also said you'd want it said twice."</npc> The pump knocks once, flat, like a ruling. Through the hatch's seam you catch a smell of condensate and hot dock metal. The voice does not mention how it knows what you carried.

*If you want to learn who this messenger really answers to, this could be a Gather Information.*

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "By when did I promise to return?"
The spoon stops halfway to your mouth. Outside, the voice takes its time.

<npc>"Before the next cargo tide,"</npc> it says. <npc>"Tamsin was particular about that. Said you'd know it was a loose word, but a firm one."</npc>

The pump knocks once against the pipes. Your hand rests on the face-down compass. The footsteps shift on the deck plating, and the voice adds, <npc>"She's closing the stall tonight. Anyone else asking for that manifest will find her already gone."</npc>

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I plot the course and take the Kobayashi IV to Bleakhold Station."
The Kobayashi IV slides into Bleakhold's docking cradle with a clean lane behind it and no tide yet turned. Clamps seat with a dull clang. The pump knocks once, steady now. Outside the viewport, corporate lamps wash the bay white, and a cargo sled idles at the next berth. A dock officer in a grey coat is already walking toward your hatch, tablet raised, saying your hull number aloud.

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "The raider cutter Ashen Wake jumps me off Bleakhold; I turn the Kobayashi IV to face it and enter the fray."
The dock officer stops mid-stride, tablet still raised, as the bay lamps flicker and a proximity tone cuts across the dock channel. Past the viewport, the *Ashen Wake* breaks from the debris shadow, closing fast. You swing the *Kobayashi IV* nose-on and read its guns hot and its heading steady. You have the angle, but you also have a hull parked half in a cradle. The pump knocks once. The dock officer's voice crackles over comms: "Hull number confirmed. Who is that behind you?"

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I'm in control, so I strike: I line up the Kobayashi IV's guns and fire at the Ashen Wake."
"Hull number confirmed," the dock officer says again, quieter now, tablet lowered. You fire, and the rounds scatter wide, chewing bay plating and nothing else. The *Ashen Wake* does not flinch. It closes on the *Kobayashi IV*, still half-seated in its cradle, and the clamps will not let go in time. The pump knocks once, flat. The officer asks, "Is that one of yours?"

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I take the hit on the chin and grit my teeth; I endure the stress of being pinned in the cradle."
You breathe out through your teeth and let the cradle's grip be what it is. The clamps hold, the hull groans, and your hands stop shaking before the panel lights stop flashing. On the comm, the dock officer asks again, flatter this time, who is behind you. The pump knocks once. Past the viewport, the *Ashen Wake* has stopped closing, its guns still hot and its nose pointed at your hatch.

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I'm in a bad spot now, so I clash: I swing the Kobayashi IV's guns around and hit the Ashen Wake head-on."
The dock officer lowers the tablet and steps back from the hatch. You swing the guns round, and this time the rounds find the *Ashen Wake*. Fresh weld seams flare along its hull, and the cutter slews off its approach, nose dragged wide. The pump knocks once. On the comm, the officer says, "Whoever that is, they're not here for the docking fee."

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "Take decisive action to seize the objective — Ashen Wake."
The *Ashen Wake* drifts clear of the bay mouth, hull scorched along its weld seams. It does not fire again. Its guns stay hot, but its pilot has stopped pushing. The pump knocks once. The dock officer finally lifts the tablet, thumb hovering. "Cutter's holding station," the officer says. "Someone wants a word with you, and it isn't me."

content.text:
You swore to find whoever is raiding the Cinder Expanse lanes, and within hours the oath had teeth. A ration clerk in Hollow Spire told you the last supply run had left before it was even posted, which meant someone had tipped the lanes. Nobody had to explain what that implied. The raiders were not guessing. They were being told.

Since then, the work has been a matter of who talks to you and who watches you. Tamsin, the ledger stall keeper wedged between a condensate filter and a shuttered chandlery, took your offer of a fair cut of the salvage and paid up front with a name: Juro, the brightly dressed man selling the lanes' timings. You paid for dock gossip and learned that the raiders hit whichever lane carries the most water, in a sector where water is rationed. Juro, for his part, has made no effort at subtlety. He was already watching when you came in, crossed the room to ask about your sister Ilse's brass star-compass, and saw you leave the cargo manifest in Tamsin's keeping. She pledged to hide it. You promised to come back before the next tide of cargo. She answered with the dry doubt of someone who has heard promises before.

The vow stands at the early marks, two boxes of ten, and the picture is still mostly shadow: a leak in the supply schedules, a seller of timings, and a set of raiders who know where the water goes. A voice outside your hatch seemed to know more than it should, reciting your promise to Tamsin, the whereabouts of your manifest, and that her stall closes tonight. It never said how it knew. Neither Tamsin nor the tipster has been made safe by any of this. You have not decided whether the voice was a warning or a threat, which is probably what it was meant to be.

Then came the bay. The Ashen Wake bore down on the Kobayashi IV while she was still locked in her cradle, and your first volley scattered wide. The second did not. You swung the guns round and struck the cutter head-on, breaking its approach and driving it off. It broke away at the bay mouth with its guns hot and silent. The Kobayashi IV is intact at five of five, and you are unhurt, with your supplies and spirit full.

Which leaves you near Bleakhold Station, a corporate holding with a smuggling problem, with a scorched ship backing off and, by the last account, someone calling at your door. The compass is still face-down in your pocket, the manifest is still under Tamsin's ledger, and the promise to return before the tide is still owed. For a vow barely begun, you have made a good many people notice you.

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I raise Tamsin on the comm again and ask how her stall is holding up, trading more news to deepen our relationship."
Outside the hatch, the visitor's boots shift once and then hold still. Tamsin's voice comes up through the comm, thinner now, the filter humming behind her. "Stall's holding. Two clerks have walked past it twice tonight and bought nothing." She lowers her voice. "I'd rather you hear it from me: someone is counting my crates." You trade what you can spare, and she keeps your words close. "Don't hang up yet," she says. "There's a name on that signature, and I know the hand."

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I ask Tamsin whose hand she knows, and offer to watch her stall tonight, deepening our relationship."
"I'll give you the name, and you'll watch the stall," Tamsin says. "But you carry my ledger off the docks first. Tonight, before the clerks come back." The filter hums behind her. "The hand is Juro's. He signs with a bright thread through the loop of the J." Her breath catches on the comm. Outside the hatch, the boots shift, and a knuckle raps once, softly, on the plating.

Tamsin's breath stops on the comm. When she speaks, the warmth has gone out of it. "A bond is a rope, Mira, and I won't tie myself to a ship the clerks are already watching." ## RECENT SCENE

The galley smells of reheated lentils and the burnt edge of a pot you keep meaning to scrub. You eat standing, one boot braced against the table leg, while Ilse's compass lies face-down by your elbow where it can't point at anything. Somewhere aft, the coolant pump knocks twice, and you decide it is the nearest thing to company you have. If the crew you don't have were aboard, you imagine the engineer would be wedged inside the number-two bulkhead again, insisting the draft was "a personality, not a leak." The cook would be taste-testing the lentils with a hull-patch spatula and filing a formal complaint against them. You tip the last of the bitter tea into your mouth and listen to the ship settle, hull ticking as it cools from the bay. A short, flat knock sounds at the hatch, polite and in no hurry.

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "Remind me, which keepsake of my sister's is on me?"
The compass answers you before anyone else does. Face-down, it still sits cold against the wood, brass scratched along one edge where Ilse thumbed it. It began at Hollow Spire, where you swore to find whoever was raiding the Cinder Expanse lanes. Within hours a ration clerk told you the last supply run had left before it was even posted. Someone had tipped the lanes. Dock gossip filled in the rest: the raiders hit whichever lane carried the most water, and a man in bright thread was already watching you. That man was Juro, who sold the lanes' timings and who crossed the room to ask whether your sister Ilse's scratched brass star-compass was for sale. It wasn't, and it still isn't. It's the one thing of hers you carry.

Tamsin Okoro, who the docks also call Tamsin Vey, wears whichever name gets her paid. She became the heart of the campaign. You offered her a fair cut of your salvage, and she paid first with word of Juro. You left your cargo manifest under her ledger, and she swore to hide it, though Juro watched the handoff. Over comm calls and a shared meal she gave you a guarded truth: three crates shipped unposted, and someone signed for them with a bright thread through the J. She refused your first offer of a bond, unwilling to tie herself to a ship the clerks were watching, then relented and agreed to say she once stood on your deck. You carried her grey-wrapped parcel, she trusted you with her secrets, and the bond is forged. It sits at full progress.

The vow is done. You laid your proof on the galley table: Juro signs for crates he never carries, he never signed for the water, and he sells the lane timings to the raiders. That was enough. You fulfilled the vow to find the Cinder Expanse raiders and set down the weight you'd carried since Hollow Spire. Along the way you fought off the Ashen Wake, a scorched cutter that bore down on you while the *Kobayashi IV* was still locked in cradle four at Bleakhold. Your first volley went wide. You swung the guns round and drove her off at the bay mouth, guns hot but silent.

The wins have left loose ends. Tamsin is closing her stall tonight and wants her ledger carried off the docks before the clerks return. By her own telling, Juro would like a rival left behind. At your hatch a stranger keeps turning up, one who knows your sister's compass by sight, knows what you promised Tamsin, and asks who wrote your tide. Nobody has explained how the stranger knows any of it.

So you are berthed at Bleakhold with a fulfilled vow, a bonded ally, and a ledger to move. Whoever stands outside your airlock has opinions about your timing, and you haven't yet answered them.

## RECENT SCENE

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "Whose hands is the manifest in these days?"
You answer aloud, a question to the hatch as much as to yourself. Tamsin's hands, last you knew, under her ledger. Hands are a stranger's word for it. "Tamsin's," you say, and the plating gives back a short pause. "That's what she'd tell you," the voice says. "Ask her where it sleeps tonight." The pump knocks once, then stops.

*If you want to read this visitor for what they're after, that could be a Gather Information.*

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "What deadline did I give for coming home to the docks?"
The visitor outside shifts again, plating creaking under a patient weight. You answer the hatch. "Before the next cargo tide. I told Tamsin that." Silence stretches, then the voice comes back, dry. "A tide is a loose word. She treats it as firm. Does the tide turn tonight, Mira, or did you let it slip?" The knock comes once more, softer. The compass lies face-down, and the pump says nothing.

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "Where is my ship berthed right now, and who commands her?"
"Berthed at Bleakhold, cradle four. You command her. Or so the dock log says," the voice answers through the hatch. You hear a datapad tap against plating. "Funny. The cutter outside holds station like it thinks otherwise." Through the galley viewport, the bay lamps show the Kobayashi IV's clamps seated and her guns cooling. The compass stays face-down. "So tell me, Mira. Did you pick this berth, or did someone pick it for you?"

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "What is the raider cutter called?"
The visitor taps the datapad once against the plating. "Cinder Wren," the voice says. "Painted on her flank, small, like someone was embarrassed by it." Through the viewport, the bay lamps catch the cutter's weld seams, fresh and bright over older marks. "You'd have read it yourself if you'd gone to look." The hatch handle turns a quarter inch and stops. "Now. Did the tide turn, Mira, or did you let it slip?"

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "What surname does my broker friend go by these days?"
The datapad stops tapping. You say it to the hatch, half a question. "Tamsin Okoro. Though the docks swear she's Vey."

The handle settles back into place. "Both are true," the voice says, easy. "Names are cheap on Hollow Spire. She wears whichever one gets her paid." Through the plating comes a slow breath. "You've kept her ledger company too long to be asking that. Did the tide turn, Mira?"

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I treat my wounds with the ship's medkit."
You pull the medkit from under the galley bench and thumb the seal. The scorched patch along your ribs takes the gel with a hiss. You bind it in silence, boot still braced on the table leg. Outside, the visitor waits, and the voice comes dry through the plating. "Hurt, then. The Cinder Wren's work, or the cradle's?" The handle turns a quarter inch again. "Answer me about the tide, Mira. I am running short of patience."

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I use the medkit to Heal my wounds properly, working the gel and bandage with care."
Open on the hatch, not you. The handle turns its quarter inch, holds, and eases back. Behind it, the visitor waits with a boot shifting against the plating.

You work the gel into the burn, lay the bandage flat, and pull the tape tight along your ribs. It stings, then settles. When you look up, the voice has changed. "Tamsin never mentioned you were this slow, Mira. Is the tide still ahead of you?"

*Reading what this visitor really wants could be a Gather Information.*

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I Heal: I use the ship's medkit on my injuries, a proper treatment."
"Better," the voice says, as if it had watched the tape go on. "You move easier. I can hear it in the deck."

The gel has taken the sting down to a dull warmth along your ribs. You roll your shoulder. Nothing tears. The bandage holds flat under your shirt, snug and clean. On the table, the compass lies face-down where you left it.

The handle does not turn this time. "Then you've no excuse left, Mira. Open the hatch, or tell me the tide has turned."

The galley smells of reheated lentils and the burnt edge of a pot you keep meaning to scrub. You eat standing, one boot braced against the table leg, while Ilse's compass lies face-down by your elbow where it can't point at anything. Somewhere aft, the coolant pump knocks twice, and you decide it is the nearest thing to company you have. If the crew you don't have were aboard, you imagine the engineer would be wedged inside the number-two bulkhead again, insisting the draft was "a personality, not a leak." The cook would be taste-testing the lentils with a hull-patch spatula and filing a formal complaint against them. You tip the last of the bitter tea into your mouth and listen to the ship settle, hull ticking as it cools from the bay. A short, flat knock sounds at the hatch, polite and in no hurry.

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "Remind me, which keepsake of my sister's is on me?"
The compass answers you before anyone else does. Face-down, it still sits cold against the wood, brass scratched along one edge where Ilse thumbed it. Then the voice comes through the hatch, low and unhurried. <npc>"The star-compass. Your sister's. I'd know that scratch anywhere."</npc> The knock does not repeat. Whoever stands outside has already said more than a stranger should know. You hear weight shift against the plating, patient.

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "Who do I count as a friend among the dock traders back where this began?"
You think of Tamsin first, then hold the thought a moment. She holds your manifest and calls you a debt. Friend is a strong word for a woman who writes everything down. Juro is no friend either, only interested. At the hatch the visitor waits, and the voice carries easily through the plating. "You're counting, aren't you? Good. Don't count me yet." The coolant pump knocks once, then goes quiet, and the compass stays face-down.

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "Whose hands is the manifest in these days?"
You answer aloud, a question to the hatch as much as to yourself. Tamsin's hands, last you knew, under her ledger. Hands are a stranger's word for it. "Tamsin's," you say, and the plating gives back a short pause. "That's what she'd tell you," the voice says. "Ask her where it sleeps tonight." The pump knocks once, then stops.

*If you want to read this visitor for what they're after, that could be a Gather Information.*

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "What deadline did I give for coming home to the docks?"
The visitor outside shifts again, plating creaking under a patient weight. You answer the hatch. "Before the next cargo tide. I told Tamsin that." Silence stretches, then the voice comes back, dry. "A tide is a loose word. She treats it as firm. Does the tide turn tonight, Mira, or did you let it slip?" The knock comes once more, softer. The compass lies face-down, and the pump says nothing.

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "Where is my ship berthed right now, and who commands her?"
"Berthed at Bleakhold, cradle four. You command her. Or so the dock log says," the voice answers through the hatch. You hear a datapad tap against plating. "Funny. The cutter outside holds station like it thinks otherwise." Through the galley viewport, the bay lamps show the Kobayashi IV's clamps seated and her guns cooling. The compass stays face-down. "So tell me, Mira. Did you pick this berth, or did someone pick it for you?"

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "What is the raider cutter called?"
The visitor taps the datapad once against the plating. "Cinder Wren," the voice says. "Painted on her flank, small, like someone was embarrassed by it." Through the viewport, the bay lamps catch the cutter's weld seams, fresh and bright over older marks. "You'd have read it yourself if you'd gone to look." The hatch handle turns a quarter inch and stops. "Now. Did the tide turn, Mira, or did you let it slip?"

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "What surname does my broker friend go by these days?"
The datapad stops tapping. You say it to the hatch, half a question. "Tamsin Okoro. Though the docks swear she's Vey."

The handle settles back into place. "Both are true," the voice says, easy. "Names are cheap on Hollow Spire. She wears whichever one gets her paid." Through the plating comes a slow breath. "You've kept her ledger company too long to be asking that. Did the tide turn, Mira?"

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I treat my wounds with the ship's medkit."
You pull the medkit from under the galley bench and thumb the seal. The scorched patch along your ribs takes the gel with a hiss. You bind it in silence, boot still braced on the table leg. Outside, the visitor waits, and the voice comes dry through the plating. "Hurt, then. The Cinder Wren's work, or the cradle's?" The handle turns a quarter inch again. "Answer me about the tide, Mira. You work the gel into the burn, lay the bandage flat, and pull the tape tight along your ribs. It stings, then settles. When you look up, the voice has changed. "Tamsin never mentioned you were this slow, Mira. Is the tide still ahead of you?"

She has trusted you with something small, and she knows it. The visitor at the hatch has heard every word. Plating creaks as a weight shifts against it.

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "One last check: what of my sister's do I have with me at this very moment?"
Your hand drops to the galley table. The brass star-compass lies face-down where you left it. It is the only thing of Ilse's aboard. You turn it over, and the scratch along its edge catches the lamp. Outside the hatch, the visitor goes quiet, as if listening to the metal. "Yes," the voice says. "That one." The needle swings and settles toward the plating, toward the voice. "Now ask me how I know it."

*Reading what this visitor truly wants could be a Gather Information.*

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "Which person in this sector would I trust with my life?"
On the comm, Tamsin has gone quiet, the filter hum filling the line. She is listening to you think.

You say it to the galley, half to yourself. One name comes without effort. Tamsin Okoro, the ledger stall, the tide you owe her. She has asked for your name to stay off her book and still stood on your deck. Trust is a heavy word for someone you have bonded with twice over.

"Don't say it aloud," Tamsin breathes. Outside the hatch, the visitor's knuckle taps once. "Ask yourself who else heard you."

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "Who has the manifest in their keeping today?"
"Tamsin has it," she says over the comm, "under the ledger, where it has been since you left." Her voice is thin. "I told you the stall closes tonight. Anyone else asking will find me gone."

The knuckle taps the hatch once. "Under the ledger," the visitor repeats, pleased. "Then someone asked her to hold it, Mira. Ask who."

*Pressing the visitor for who set that deadline would be a Gather Information.*

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "On what schedule did I swear to come back to her?"
Your own words come back to you: *before the next cargo tide*. Tamsin takes them off the comm. "That was it. Before the tide, no sooner, no later." The filter hums behind her. "I never named the hour. Someone else did."

Outside the hatch, the visitor stops tapping. A boot scuffs the plating, once.

"Careful," the voice says. "Ask who gave her that tide."

*Pressing Tamsin on who set that deadline would be a Gather Information.*

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "Which station are we docked at tonight?"
Open on Tamsin, not the hatch. Her answer comes over the comm, flat and quick. "Bleakhold. You docked there yourself, Mira. Hull number read at the cradle, clamps still seated." The filter hums behind her.

You glance at the bay lamps through the galley port. The Cinder Wren holds station beyond them, patient.

Outside the hatch, the visitor chuckles once. "She's answering the easy questions. Ask her who set the hour."

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "What was the hostile vessel in our last battle christened?"
"The Cinder Wren," Tamsin says over the comm. "Painted small on her flank, near the weld seams. You'd have to be close to read it." The filter hums behind her.

Through the galley port, the cutter holds beyond the bay lamps. Her name is a scratch of white on dark plating.

Outside the hatch, the visitor stays quiet a moment. "Everyone knows her name by now," the voice says. "Ask who taught her yours."

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "What is my bonded friend's full name now?"
Tamsin answers over the comm, dry and unhurried. "Okoro. Tamsin Okoro. The docks call me Vey, and I answer to it when it pays." The filter hums behind her.

Outside the hatch, the visitor laughs once, softly. "Both names are true," the voice says. "She wears whichever one gets her paid." The knuckle taps the plating. "Ask which name wrote your tide."

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "Didn't I leave the compass with Tamsin?"
"You did not," Tamsin says over the comm. "It's face-down on your galley table, where you keep leaving it." The filter hums behind her.

You look. The brass is cold under your palm, the scratch along its edge bright in the lamp.

Outside the hatch, the visitor laughs once, low. "Then who put that idea in your head, Mira? Ask her."

*Pressing Tamsin on who set that deadline would be a Gather Information.*

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "We are still docked at Hollow Spire, aren't we?"
"No," Tamsin says over the comm. "Bleakhold. Cradle four, clamps seated. Hollow Spire is where you left me." The filter hums behind her, the sound of a stall that has not closed yet.

Through the galley port, the bay lamps burn steady and the Wren holds beyond them.

Outside the hatch, the visitor tuts. "You mixed your stations, Mira. Someone has you turned around."

The knuckle raps once. "Who's been telling you where you are?"

content.text:
You swore to find the Cinder Expanse raiders at Hollow Spire, and within hours a ration clerk was telling you the last supply run had left before it was ever posted. Someone had tipped the lanes. That was the whole case at the start: raiders who struck whichever lane carried the most water, and an inside voice feeding them the schedule. Dock gossip cost you coin, and it cost you a watcher in bright thread, who noticed you before you had finished noticing him.

The watcher was Juro, and the long middle of the campaign was spent on him and on the woman who named him. Tamsin Okoro keeps a ledger stall on the Hollow Spire docks and trades under the name Vey when it pays better. She was a hard sell. She took a fair cut of your salvage, refused your first offer of a bond, then relented and let you carry her grey-wrapped parcel, trade confidences over the comm, and share a meal. Now the bond is full, which is more than most people on those docks can say of anyone. She holds your cargo manifest under her ledger, and you put her name first when you were asked whom you would trust with your life. Whether that trust is well placed, a stranger at your hatch has been politely asking.

The vow itself is done. You proved that Juro signs for crates he never carries and sells the lane timings to the raiders. You laid out the crates, the looped J, and the hour of each run on your galley table, and Tamsin went quiet on the line. That fulfilled the oath you swore, and you set the weight down. Along the way you drove off the Ashen Wake in a bay fight that began badly and ended well, and you learned the hostile vessel's other name, the Cinder Wren.

The revelations since have been less welcome. The man at your hatch knows your sister Ilse's scratched brass star-compass on sight, the one thing of hers you still carry, and he talks as though your memory has been tampered with. You believed you had left the compass with Tamsin, but it was on your own galley table all along. You believed you were berthed at Hollow Spire, but the dock log puts the Kobayashi IV at Bleakhold, cradle four, with you as captain. Even your promise to return to Tamsin before the next cargo tide has a problem: Tamsin never named that hour, and someone else did. A cutter outside seems to disagree about who is in charge of your own ship.

So you sit at Bleakhold Station, a corporate-run place with a smuggling problem, hull at full integrity, supplies and spirit intact, and a vow fulfilled. The raiders have a name and a source, and your friend is bonded to you. What remains open is the stranger's question, which keeps coming back to who wrote your tide, and who has been editing what you remember of it.
